That list had fallen out of date more than once, and some callers skipped the `As*` helpers entirely by type-asserting agents directly, which also skipped the declaration check.\n\nThis PR makes the list and the helpers enforceable, so reviewers no longer have to keep them in sync by hand.\n\n## What changed\n\nEvery package-level `As*` capability helper now resolves through one of three standard functions:\n\n- `declaredCapability`: a `CapabilityDeclarer` must implement the interface and declare the matching `DeclaredCaps` field.\n- `builtinCapability`: implementing the interface is enough; there is no `DeclaredCaps` field to check.\n- `nonDeclarerCapability`: `CapabilityDeclarer` agents are refused even if they implement the interface (`LateTranscriptWriter`, `OutOfBandTokenSource`).\n\n`nonDeclarerCapability` replaces two hand-written copies of the same logic. # General review lessons

- When deciding whether to hide or drop something, recognize the safe case from a short list of known phrasings rather than listing the unsafe ones; a list of unsafe words always misses some phrasing, and a false "safe" hides real information.
- Match keywords on whole words, not string prefixes; `HasPrefix(s, "with no")` also matches "with notes".
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model; any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path; otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
# cli review lessons

- If `InstallHooks` can rewrite an agent's config without adding hooks, report it through `StaleHookReporter`; `count == 0` alone prints "already installed", which hides the rewrite.

content.text:
The PR is in good shape, and the latest committed head (`6262d68`) has green CI. Your uncommitted guard changes leave a few gaps, though. Two are worth fixing before you push.

**What I checked**
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/` passes with your local changes applied.
- I ran the guard against probe files in a throwaway clone outside the worktree. Your worktree is unchanged.
- I didn't run lint because another `golangci-lint` process was already running. I also didn't rerun `mise run check`.
- The branch has no Entire Trail, so there were no Trail findings to check.

**Findings**

1. **The guard can still be bypassed three ways (confirmed).** I put this file in an untracked package. The guard passed all three assertions and caught only the interface literal:
   ```go
   type aliasHS = agent.HookSupport
   type definedHS agent.HookSupport
   _, _ = ag.(aliasHS)      // missed
   _, _ = ag.(definedHS)    // missed
   _, _ = ag.(zzp1.Hooky)   // missed; zzp1: type Hooky interface{ agent.HookSupport }
   ```
   The cause is that `declaredInterfaces` only records type specs that are interface literals. `asInterfaceType` only resolves names declared in the same package. Both new comments (the test doc and `testing.md`) suggest the guard covers more than this.

   I recommend two fixes:
   - Make `declaredInterfaces` also record alias and defined types that name an `agent` interface.
   - Resolve `pkg.X` by mapping the import path to a repo directory and looking it up in `localInterfaces`. That's about 15 lines and fits the existing pattern.

   I wouldn't switch to `go/types`, because it would need `golang.org/x/tools`, a new dependency.

2. **The "gone stale" check depends on a single line of code.** It now counts only assertions to allowed interfaces outside package `agent`.
